points.point: The Vault's signal integrity capability list is a high-speed PCB/PCBA flow: IL / Xtalk / eye diagram, TDR impedance, Stackup Planner, TL Calculator — not a wireless-application list.
points.label: missing
points.why: does not give IL/Xtalk/eye/TDR/Stackup Planner/TL Calculator or say this is a PCB/PCBA, not wireless, list

points.point: Signal Integrity is positioned in the Digital / high-speed digital test context, with RF as a separate target category, so the Vault does not frame SI as a wireless-communication capability area.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: frames SI capabilities as wireless-communication capabilities instead of noting SI is treated as digital/high-speed digital with RF separate

points.point: In the R&S PCB test solutions flow, Signal Integrity modeling/testing is defined as IL, DK/DF, roughness and impedance.
points.label: partial
points.why: mentions SI modeling/testing but not its definition as IL, DK/DF, roughness and impedance

points.point: The only wireless-infrastructure SI reference is O-RU / Open RAN testing, where "Timing / Sync / Signal Integrity" is listed as one key test focus area.
points.label: missing
points.why: does not mention O-RU/Open RAN or Timing / Sync / Signal Integrity focus area

points.point: In the Jio mmWave (Wi-Fi over mmWave) project, signal integrity is tied to EVM/modulation-quality tuning after signal up-conversion.
points.label: covered
points.why: includes Jio mmWave, EVM/modulation quality tuning, and SI after up-conversion

points.point: In an SDR/UAV wireless review, filtering stages plus configurable AGC are what mitigate interference and maintain signal integrity.
points.label: missing
points.why: does not mention SDR/UAV filtering stages or configurable AGC maintaining SI

invented: Wireless SI work should support verification of 3GPP mmWave-related test items.
